original_reference_provenance.finding: Historical CUDA.jl already implements the complex convolution and native warp reduction. It uses Float64 floor/bins instead of native floorf, guards image loads before bounds rather than using padded source storage, and sorts by kernel sub-bin order rather than the native swapped-axis locality key. These are precision/input/memory mapping differences, not evidence of a wrong configured scientific operator. Named adapter aligns Float32 floorf and fully initialized padded storage.
original_reference_provenance.named_configuration: Guarded-header macros NPOINTS64 IMG_SIZE64 GCF_DIM32 REPEAT3; GCF_GRID8 and 32×8 source geometry retained. Two generated dyadic fixtures replace source default random/transcendental inputs.
original_reference_provenance.point_sort_scope: Named comparator uses floor fractions and swapped-axis key. It agrees with source modf comparator for nonnegative points, but differs for negative coordinates included here. The study_common source comment about native ordering is qualified by this statement. All four consume the same complete serialized ordered point list.
